clue.text: Scruffy slob Isaac, pop artist

indicators.note: scruffy means untidy and dishevelled, so the letters that follow are left in a messy new order

blocks.note: the letters of these three words are the fodder

explanation.surface: A sneer at a scruffy pop-art painter who is a slob called Isaac.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pop artist' reads as one phrase, but 'pop' belongs to the fodder and only 'artist' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Pablo Picasso, the Spanish painter who co-founded Cubism, is among the most famous artists of the twentieth century.

clue.text: Stretches Achilles' tendon, initially beset by painful complaint

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each of the two words before it
to be beset by something is to be surrounded by it, so the selected letters sit inside the next piece

blocks.note: piles are haemorrhoids, a painful complaint
first letters of Achilles and tendon

explanation.surface: A sports injury: stretching an Achilles tendon brings on a painful condition.
explanation.walkthrough: PILES opens to take AT: PIL(AT)ES.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilates is an exercise regime built on controlled stretches and core strengthening, so the plural noun fits.

clue.text: Something from the bakery, gift of French orator sent round?

indicators.note: sending something round turns it about, so the joined pieces are read from the end backwards

blocks.note: le is French for 'the'

explanation.surface: A baker's treat presented as a present from some French public speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gift of the gab' is the idiom for a talent for fluent speech, so the orator supplies only the gab.
explanation.definitionFit: A bagel is a ring-shaped bread roll, boiled then baked, so it is a bakery product.

clue.text: Composer spoiled every single note penned

indicators.note: penned means shut in a pen, so the note is enclosed by the word for every single

blocks.note: food that has spoiled has gone off
each means every single one

explanation.surface: A critic complains that a composer ruined every single note he wrote.
explanation.walkthrough: NB, Latin nota bene, is a note in the sense of a written reminder, not a musical one.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacques Offenbach was the German-French composer of operettas such as Orpheus in the Underworld and the can-can tune.

clue.text: Religious leader, married, got in an hour after midnight

indicators.note: something that has got in has entered, so the abbreviation for married sits inside the time

blocks.note: one o'clock in the morning is 1 a.m., read as I AM
M is the standard abbreviation for married

explanation.surface: A cleric who has just married comes home at one in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: The roman numeral I stands for 1, so 1 a.m. becomes IAM, with M slipped in: I(M)AM.
explanation.definitionFit: An imam is the man who leads prayers in a mosque, a Muslim religious leader.

clue.text: Vamp undressed Boris after cooking a delicious meal

indicators.note: undressed means stripped of its outer covering, so only the inner letters of the word stay
cooking changes raw ingredients into something else, so these letters are mixed up

taken as written, fodder for the mix
taken as written, added to the fodder

explanation.definitionFit: Ambrosia is the food of the gods in Greek myth, so it stands for any delicious meal.

clue.text: Fur bishop found in stock clearance

B is bishop in chess notation

explanation.definitionFit: Sable is the prized dark pelt of a small Asian marten, a luxury fur.

clue.text: Roll Over Mozart: a classic case for rock?

indicators.note: a case holds something inside it, so the letters are cased within the words just before
rolling over turns something upside down, so the concealed letters run backwards

blocks.note: the run inside moZART A CLAssic

explanation.walkthrough: 'Roll Over Mozart' plays on Chuck Berry's 'Roll Over Beethoven'. The prison is nicknamed The Rock, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Alcatraz, the island prison in San Francisco Bay, was known as The Rock.

clue.text: Grant established in area of E London

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the name of the London district

blocks.note: Bow is a district in the East End of London
est. is the abbreviation for established, as on shop signs

explanation.surface: A grant has been set up in a part of east London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grant' could be a name or a noun; here it is the verb, to give.
explanation.definitionFit: To bestow is to confer or give formally, which is what grant means as a verb.

clue.text: Joint's small bricks Florida doctor bonded

blocks.note: Lego is the toy made of small plastic bricks
Fla is an abbreviation for Florida
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A joint construction where toy bricks and a Florida doctor are stuck together.
explanation.definitionFit: A leg of lamb is a joint of meat for roasting, the butcher's sense of joint.

clue.text: Rubbish left in sack

indicators.note: in puts the abbreviation for left inside the phrase meaning sack

blocks.note: to be given the big E (the elbow) is to be sacked
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Somebody's rubbish has been left behind in a bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sack' looks like a bag, but it means dismissal: getting the big E, British slang for being given the elbow, or fired.
explanation.definitionFit: Bilge, from the dirty water in a ship's hull, is slang for nonsense or worthless rubbish.

clue.text: Gift Stan unwrapped fast

blocks.note: Stan without its first and last letters

explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' looks like speed; it is the fast of Lent.
explanation.definitionFit: A talent is a natural gift or aptitude for something.

clue.text: Predict Spooner's heart racing?

blocks.note: heart is core and racing is fast; swapping their opening sounds gives the result

explanation.surface: A question about whether one can tell in advance that a heart will race.
explanation.definitionFit: To forecast is to predict, as with the weather.

clue.text: Second best joke

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
the cream is the best part

explanation.surface: A ranking of gags: this is the second-best joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is a scream is hilariously funny, so the noun can stand for a joke.

clue.text: Make fresh eggs tenant mostly eats

clue.text: Hard right exposed former PM, almost intellectual

blocks.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
right without its outer letters

clue.text: Ah … the Alps! Sporty holiday here!

explanation.definitionFit: A health spa is a resort where people go on holiday for treatments, exercise and relaxation.

clue.text: Resent, for example, King checked by move

explanation.definitionFit: To begrudge someone something is to resent their having it.

clue.text: Back up north, nouveau riche more aggressive

indicators.note: back means going in the opposite direction, so the next short word runs from its end

blocks.note: taken as written, then turned round

taken as written, fodder for the mix

explanation.surface: Up north, the newly wealthy are becoming more pushy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nouveau riche' reads as one phrase, but nouveau only signals that riche is rearranged.

clue.text: Dad tense when smuggling designer drug parcel

explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer Goldsmith' suggests Oliver Goldsmith the author, but this is Zac, the politician.

clue.text: Might it help open American Indian watering hole?

definitions.text: Might it help open American Indian watering hole?

blocks.note: the Crow are a Native American people of Montana

clue.text: Crones sample place notable for bareback riding

clue.text: City state hosting African politicians
